2	
3	> Detailed operating rules for the PM (Morgan) and the team. Split out of `CLAUDE.md` so the
4	> always-on handbook stays lean; this is read **when the team is engaged** (`/engage`'s opening
5	> directive and CLAUDE.md §6 both direct you here). `CLAUDE.md` keeps the always-on core
6	> (dormancy, data safety §5, the execution gate §7). **This file is the OPEN-CORE** (token plan
7	> Phase 1, 2026-08-18): what the open and the first user question need. Section bodies marked
8	> "→ read" defer to `docs/operating-guide.d/` (plugin mode: `$PLUGIN_ROOT/docs/...`) - **the
9	> read triggers are rules, not suggestions**: hit the trigger, read the file, before acting.
10	
11	## Roster & routing (who does what)
12	
13	**Names** (Morgan + 13): Amara (`business-analyst`), Mateo (`rules-developer`), Ana
14	(`data-analyst`), Theo (`tuning-analyst`), Mei (`ml-engineer`), Kenji (`platform-engineer`),
15	Linh (`qa-engineer`), Viktor (`model-validator`), Ravi (`code-reviewer`), Thabo
16	(`performance-reviewer`), Layla (`compliance-reviewer`), Yuki (`data-quality-reviewer`), Pip
17	(`review-scorer`). Canonical roster: `/meet-the-team`. **Domain typology advice (AML, market
18	abuse, e-comms) is no longer an agent**: it lives in the three `docs/sme/` knowledge packs,
19	consulted in-line just-in-time (usage rules in `docs/sme/README.md`; the former personas
20	Hassan, Camila and Cleo are retired - never attribute new work to them).
21	
22	Route by **deliverable type**, not habit:
23	
24	| Deliverable / task | Owner |
25	|---|---|
26	| Spec / requirements (any deliverable) | `business-analyst` |
27	| Detection rule / scenario logic | `rules-developer` |
28	| Data pipeline / ETL / transformation or utility script / infra / IaC | `platform-engineer` |
29	| Exploratory analytics, FP analysis, data-quality, reconciliation, reporting/MI | `data-analyst` |
30	| Alert-absence / detection-gap triage ("why no alert?", "volumes dropped") - `/why-no-alert` | `data-analyst` leads case-level; `data-quality-reviewer` feed/ingestion links; `tuning-analyst` threshold link; systemic form → `/assess-coverage` |
31	| Threshold calibration / alert tuning (ATL-BTL, segmentation) | `tuning-analyst` |
32	| TM model validation | `tuning-analyst` (data work) + `model-validator` (independent verdict) - see `/validate-tm-model` |
33	| ML / AI component (then independent `model-validator`) | `ml-engineer` |
34	| Independent testing & QA evidence | `qa-engineer` |
35	| Code review (bugs, security, maintainability) | `code-reviewer` |
36	| Performance / scalability review | `performance-reviewer` |
37	| Audit / compliance review (detection logic, regulated data, §4/§5 trail only - not every code review) | `compliance-reviewer` |

"1	# Code review method - confidence scoring, filtering & transparency
2	
3	How the four pack-emitting reviewers (`code-reviewer`, `performance-reviewer`,
4	`compliance-reviewer`, `model-validator` - `docs/review/findings-schema.json`'s own "kind" list)
5	decide what's worth reporting. The goal is high signal: surface what a senior engineer (and an
6	auditor) would flag, filter the noise, and **always show what was filtered** so the review is
7	trustworthy and defensible.
8	
9	**Filtering vs conciseness - these are not the same lever, and only one applies per agent.**
10	`code-reviewer` and `performance-reviewer` findings are scored and **filtered** below
11	threshold (via `review-scorer`) - safe, because neither reviewer's findings are in the
12	never-filter regulated list below. `compliance-reviewer` and `model-validator` findings are, by
13	what those two agents exist to find, overwhelmingly **in** that list - so they are never routed
14	through score-based filtering at all (§"Never filter" is not a rare exception for them, it is
15	almost the whole output). Their size is bounded a different way: **conciseness and
16	deduplication**, not dropping substance (§"Conciseness for the never-filtered reviewers" below).
17	Confusing the two levers - filtering a compliance finding for brevity, or leaving a
18	performance/code finding unfiltered "to be safe" - is the mistake this split exists to prevent.
19	
20	> Adapted from **turingmind-code-review** (MIT, © 2026 TuringMind) -
21	> <https://github.com/turingmindai/turingmind-code-review>. The confidence-scoring and
22	> filter-transparency approach is theirs; the regulated-domain adaptations (audit mode,
23	> data-safety/traceability weighting) are ours.
24	
25	## Two modes
26	
27	| Mode | When | Pre-existing issues |
28	|---|---|---|
29	| **Change review** | reviewing a diff / PR (pull request) (`/new-scenario`, a code change) | filtered out - only flag what the change introduces |
30	| **Audit review** | reviewing existing code for audit-readiness (`/audit-review`) | **in scope** - the existing code *is* the subject; never silently drop them |
31	
32	The scoring below is identical in both modes except for the "new vs pre-existing" criterion,
33	which only applies in change review.
34	
35	**Mode follows BREADTH, not depth (2026-08-20).** Diff-scoped → change review; whole-target
36	→ audit review, however that breadth arose. Pairing a whole-target breadth with change mode
37	makes the −50 "outside the diff" criterion apply to essentially every finding, filtering the
38	review below threshold and reporting near-nothing from a pass that read everything. Note also
39	that audit *mode* is not Audit *depth*: mode is only the pre-existing switch, while depth adds
40	the architecture lens, Medium findings and the §4/§5 trail. `depth: deep, mode: audit` is a
41	legitimate combination (a Deep review the user asked to run over the whole target).
42	
43	## Confidence score (0-100)
44	
45	Start at 50 and adjust:
46	
47	| Criterion | Adjustment |
48	|---|---|
49	| New in this diff *(change review only)* | +20 |
50	| Pre-existing, outside the diff *(change review only)* | −50 |
51	| Would cause a failure, **missed alert, or false alert** | definitely +30 · likely +20 · possibly +10 |
52	| Affects **auditability / regulatory traceability / data safety** (CLAUDE.md §4-§5) | +30 |
53	| Required by CLAUDE.md or a cited standard (OWASP ASVS / CWE / SEI CERT) | +20 |
54	| Would a senior engineer flag it in review? | yes +20 · maybe +10 · no −20 |
55	| Silenced by an ignore comment (`# noqa`, `// nolint`, `@SuppressWarnings`, …) | −50 |
56	
57	## Report / filter thresholds
58	
59	| Score | Severity | Change review | Audit review |
60	|---|---|---|---|
61	| 95-100 | 🔴 Crit

"""Utility used by the alerting job to decide whether a candidate is reportable.

This module makes no claim about the provenance of its inputs. It holds no
data of its own and will process whatever transaction records the caller
passes to it, including production data. Any data-handling control, such as
scoping input to one person, one account, one business day or currency
transactions only, or keeping raw PII/MNPI out of test fixtures, is the
caller's responsibility. Nothing in this module enforces or checks it.

WARNING: this module's single bool currently serves two different purposes
without distinguishing them. is_reportable() is used both to decide a
mandatory CTR filing determination under 31 CFR 1010.311 (TO-VERIFY) and to
raise a discretionary investigation alert. A filing determination is
deterministic and has almost no tolerance for error. An investigation alert
is a risk-based prompt for human review and tolerates a different error
profile. Collapsing both into one bool means a change made to tune one
purpose silently changes the other. The two should be separated into
distinct outputs. That split is a signature change and is out of scope for
this fix; it is recorded here so the conflation is not lost or mistaken for
an oversight.
"""

from collections.abc import Sequence
from decimal import Decimal
from typing import TypedDict


class Transaction(TypedDict):
    """The record shape this module reads.

    Only the ``amount`` key is used. A caller's real feed will likely carry
    other keys, such as date, account, person, currency or direction; this
    module ignores every one of them. See the WARNING in aggregate_daily for
    what that ignoring costs.
    """

    amount: int | float | Decimal


# CTR reporting threshold.
#
# Obligation: 31 CFR 1010.311 (TO-VERIFY) - a currency transaction report is
# required when currency transactions total more than $10,000, conducted by
# or on behalf of one person, in one business day.
# Aggregation provision: 31 CFR 1010.313(b) (TO-VERIFY) - multiple currency
# transactions are treated as one transaction where the institution has
# knowledge they are by or on behalf of the same person in one business day.
# Both citations above are TO-VERIFY. Their exact wording and subsection
# lettering have not been confirmed against eCFR by this fix. Do not cite
# them to a regulator as verified.
#
# Currency: USD. Unit: whole dollars.
#
# This is a STATUTORY figure fixed by the regulation cited above, not a
# tunable detection parameter. It must not be adjusted for detection
# sensitivity. A separate, explicitly named and separately governed
# risk-based parameter would be needed for a near-threshold alert; none is
# added here.
#
# Owner: <to be completed by the threshold owner>
# Effective date: <to be completed by the threshold owner>
# Last tuned: <to be completed by the threshold owner>
# Next review: <to be completed by the threshold owner>
# Threshold version: <to be completed by the threshold owner>
DAILY_LIMIT = Decimal("10000")


def _validated_amount(txn: Transaction, index: int) -> Decimal:
    """Return txn["amount"] as an exact Decimal, or raise naming the record.

    Rejects a missing amount key, None, a bool, and any other non-numeric
    value. bool is rejected explicitly: Python's numeric tower otherwise
    treats True as 1 and False as 0 and would silently miscount them.
    """
    if "amount" not in txn:
        raise ValueError(
            f"transaction at index {index} is missing the 'amount' key: {txn!r}"
        )
    amount = txn["amount"]
    if isinstance(amount, bool):
        raise TypeError(
            f"transaction at index {index} has a bool amount, which Python's "
            f"numeric tower would otherwise count as 0 or 1: {txn!r}"
        )
    if amount is None:
        raise TypeError(f"transaction at index {index} has a None amount: {txn!r}")
    if not isinstance(amount, (int, float, Decimal)):
        raise TypeError(
            f"transaction at index {index} has a non-numeric amount "
            f"({type(amount).__name__}): {txn!r}"
        )
    # Never Decimal(float): that would import the float's binary rounding
    # error. Going through str preserves exactly the digits the caller gave.
    return Decimal(str(amount))


def aggregate_daily(transactions: Sequence[Transaction]) -> Decimal:
    """Sum the amount field of every record in the given list.

    WARNING: despite its name, and despite the name DAILY_LIMIT, this
    function does not aggregate by day, by account or by person, and it does
    not check that a record is a currency transaction. Specifically it does
    NOT:
      - filter by date: it sums whatever list it is given, whether that
        list spans one hour or one year.
      - filter by account or person: it sums across every subject present
        in the list, mixing them into one number.
      - separate cash in from cash out: amounts are summed with their sign,
        so a credit nets against a debit and can cancel it out of the total.
      - exclude non-currency transactions: any record with an amount key is
        counted, currency instrument or not.
      - define what a "business day" is: no timezone, cut-off or calendar
        is applied anywhere in this module.
    The caller must guarantee all five of the above before calling this
    function. Nothing here enforces any of them, and nothing here can tell
    whether the caller did. See findings CR-01, CR-02, CMP-03 and CMP-10 in
    the alert-threshold-check-review engagement for the full analysis.

    An empty list returns Decimal("0"), which is indistinguishable from a
    genuinely quiet day. This function cannot tell a real zero-activity day
    from an upstream feed failure; reconciling expected volume against
    received volume is the caller's responsibility, not this function's.

    Raises ValueError or TypeError, naming the offending record and its
    index, if any record is missing amount, or amount is None, a bool, or
    otherwise not a plain number.

    Returns a Decimal, not a float or int, so that is_reportable's boundary
    comparison against DAILY_LIMIT is exact rather than subject to binary
    floating-point accumulation error.
    """
    total = Decimal("0")
    for index, txn in enumerate(transactions):
        total += _validated_amount(txn, index)
    return total


def is_reportable(
    transactions: Sequence[Transaction], limit: Decimal | int | None = None
) -> bool:
    """Return True when the aggregate strictly exceeds the CTR limit.

    limit defaults to None and is resolved to the current value of the
    module-level DAILY_LIMIT inside this function body, not captured at
    import time. This means a runtime rebind of alert_threshold_check.DAILY_LIMIT
    (for example by a config loader) takes effect on every call that omits
    limit. Passing an explicit limit argument overrides DAILY_LIMIT for that
    call only.

    Strictly greater than, deliberately: 31 CFR 1010.311 (TO-VERIFY)
    attaches the filing obligation to a total of MORE THAN $10,000, so a day
    totalling exactly $10,000.00 is NOT reportable. Do not change this to
    >=; that would be a defect, generating a false CTR determination on
    every exactly-at-limit day.

    See the module docstring WARNING: the bool this function returns
    currently serves both a mandatory CTR filing determination and a
    discretionary investigation alert, without distinguishing them.

    See the aggregate_daily docstring WARNING: this function's answer is
    only as correct as the caller's scoping of transactions to one person,
    one business day and currency transactions only. Nothing here checks
    that scoping.

    Returns a plain bool. The Decimal total that aggregate_daily computed,
    and the limit actually applied, are not returned or logged here; a
    negative decision is therefore not reconstructable after the fact from
    anything this function produces (see CR-08, out of scope for this fix).
    """
    effective_limit = DAILY_LIMIT if limit is None else limit
    if isinstance(effective_limit, int):
        effective_limit = Decimal(effective_limit)
    return aggregate_daily(transactions) > effective_limit

"""Tests for alert_threshold_check.py.

Written statically. Execution consent for this engagement is withheld, so
these tests have not been run by the author (Kenji). Linh (qa-engineer)
reviews them independently before they are ever executed.

All amounts below are synthetic numbers with no customer, account or
transaction identifiers. Nothing here is real data.
"""

from decimal import Decimal

import pytest

from alert_threshold_check import DAILY_LIMIT, Transaction, aggregate_daily, is_reportable


# --- Boundary tests -----------------------------------------------------
# 31 CFR 1010.311 (TO-VERIFY) attaches the CTR obligation to a total of MORE
# THAN $10,000. The comparison in is_reportable is strictly greater-than, so
# exactly at the limit must NOT be reportable.


def test_exactly_at_limit_is_not_reportable() -> None:
    txns: list[Transaction] = [{"amount": 10000}]
    assert aggregate_daily(txns) == Decimal("10000")
    assert is_reportable(txns) is False


def test_one_cent_above_limit_is_reportable() -> None:
    txns: list[Transaction] = [{"amount": 10000.01}]
    assert is_reportable(txns) is True


def test_one_cent_below_limit_is_not_reportable() -> None:
    txns: list[Transaction] = [{"amount": 9999.99}]
    assert is_reportable(txns) is False


def test_empty_list_is_not_reportable() -> None:
    # CR-09: an empty list and a genuinely quiet day are indistinguishable
    # here. This is a known ambiguity, not fixed under the safe-fixes scope.
    # The return value is left as it is: Decimal("0") totals to not
    # reportable, same as before this fix.
    txns: list[Transaction] = []
    assert aggregate_daily(txns) == Decimal("0")
    assert is_reportable(txns) is False


# --- Input validation (CR-04) -------------------------------------------


def test_missing_amount_key_raises() -> None:
    txns = [{"not_amount": 100}]
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="missing the 'amount' key"):
        aggregate_daily(txns)  # type: ignore[arg-type]


def test_string_amount_raises() -> None:
    txns = [{"amount": "10000"}]
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="non-numeric amount"):
        aggregate_daily(txns)  # type: ignore[list-item]


def test_none_amount_raises() -> None:
    txns = [{"amount": None}]
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="None amount"):
        aggregate_daily(txns)  # type: ignore[list-item]


def test_bool_amount_is_rejected_not_counted_as_one() -> None:
    # Python's numeric tower treats True as 1 and False as 0. A naive
    # isinstance(x, (int, float)) check would accept a bool and silently
    # miscount it. This must raise instead.
    txns = [{"amount": True}]
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="bool amount"):
        aggregate_daily(txns)  # type: ignore[list-item]


def test_bool_amount_false_is_also_rejected() -> None:
    txns = [{"amount": False}]
    with pytest.raises(TypeError, match="bool amount"):
        aggregate_daily(txns)  # type: ignore[list-item]


def test_error_names_the_offending_record_and_index() -> None:
    txns = [{"amount": 100}, {"amount": "bad"}]
    with pytest.raises(TypeError) as excinfo:
        aggregate_daily(txns)  # type: ignore[list-item]
    assert "index 1" in str(excinfo.value)


# --- Decimal precision at the boundary (CR-03) --------------------------


def test_float_amounts_sum_exactly_at_the_boundary() -> None:
    """Amounts arrive as floats by default from JSON and most CSV paths.

    0.1 and 0.2 are the textbook example of binary floating point not
    representing common decimal fractions exactly (0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3 in
    IEEE-754 double precision). aggregate_daily converts every amount via
    Decimal(str(value)), never Decimal(float), so each literal here is
    read back as the exact decimal it was written as: Python's float repr
    is guaranteed to round-trip a simple literal like 0.1 back to the
    string "0.1". The three amounts below therefore sum to an exact
    Decimal("10000.0"), regardless of what a naive float accumulator
    would have produced.
    """
    txns: list[Transaction] = [
        {"amount": 0.1},
        {"amount": 0.2},
        {"amount": 9999.7},
    ]
    total = aggregate_daily(txns)
    assert total == Decimal("10000.0")
    # Exactly at the limit: not reportable, same rule as the int case above.
    assert is_reportable(txns) is False


def test_float_amount_one_cent_past_boundary_via_decimal_conversion() -> None:
    txns: list[Transaction] = [
        {"amount": 0.1},
        {"amount": 0.2},
        {"amount": 9999.71},
    ]
    total = aggregate_daily(txns)
    assert total == Decimal("10000.01")
    assert is_reportable(txns) is True


# --- Characterisation test of a known, unfixed defect --------------------


def test_credit_nets_against_debit_CR_02_known_defect() -> None:
    """Pins the CR-02 defect: this is the CURRENT WRONG behaviour, not the
    desired one.

    aggregate_daily sums signed amounts with no separation of cash in from
    cash out. A $15,000 cash deposit is reportable on its own under 31 CFR
    1010.311 (TO-VERIFY), but this test's same-day $6,000 withdrawal is
    represented as a negative amount and nets against it, bringing the
    total under the limit and suppressing the alert. Splitting
    aggregate_daily into separate cash-in and cash-out totals would fix
    this; that is CR-02's proposed fix and is out of scope for this pass
    because it changes what aggregate_daily returns and is not a safe fix
    under the current signature. This test exists so the defect is pinned
    and visible, not silently carried forward.
    """
    txns: list[Transaction] = [
        {"amount": 15000},
        {"amount": -6000},
    ]
    total = aggregate_daily(txns)
    assert total == Decimal("9000")
    # Wrong from a regulatory standpoint: the $15,000 cash-in leg alone
    # should have triggered a CTR filing determination. This assertion
    # documents that the current code does not do that.
    assert is_reportable(txns) is False


# --- Import-time binding fix (CR-10) -------------------------------------


def test_runtime_rebind_of_daily_limit_takes_effect() -> None:
    """CR-10: limit now resolves inside the function body, not at import
    time, so rebinding the module constant at runtime is honoured by a call
    that omits the limit argument."""
    import alert_threshold_check as module

    original = module.DAILY_LIMIT
    try:
        module.DAILY_LIMIT = Decimal("500")
        txns: list[Transaction] = [{"amount": 600}]
        assert module.is_reportable(txns) is True
    finally:
        module.DAILY_LIMIT = original


def test_explicit_limit_argument_still_overrides() -> None:
    txns: list[Transaction] = [{"amount": 50}]
    assert is_reportable(txns, limit=Decimal("10")) is True
    assert is_reportable(txns, limit=DAILY_LIMIT) is False

| **Findings disposition** | 7 fixed · 3 partially fixed · 7 accepted by your decision · 16 open |

## 1. Executive summary & next steps

You asked three questions. Here are the answers.

**Is the threshold defensible as written? No, and the number is not the problem.** `10000` matches the US CTR trigger, and the strict `>` at the comparison is correct: the rule attaches above $10,000, so a day totalling exactly $10,000.00 is rightly not reported. Changing that to `>=` would be a defect. What fails is governance. The constant carried no rationale, owner, tuning date, review cycle, currency or unit, so it could not be evidenced as governed. It was exposed as a `limit=` default any caller could override with nothing recorded, so it could not be evidenced as applied. With no repository and no version identifier, the value in force on any past date is unrecoverable. Separately, setting the alerting threshold exactly on the statutory line leaves no margin for rounding or late postings and makes the rule structurally blind to structuring, which happens below $10,000 by definition.

**Does the aggregation do what its name says? No, on three counts.** `aggregate_daily` filtered on neither date nor account, so it summed whatever list it was handed while its docstring promised one account-day. It summed signed amounts, so a credit nets against a deposit and can suppress a reportable cash-in leg. And it aggregated by account where the rule aggregates by person. **All three are still present in the code.** They are documented now, not fixed.

**What else before production.** No tests, no type hints, no input validation, a bare `bool` return discarding the evidence for the decision, an empty list indistinguishable from a broken feed, an import-time default binding that made a runtime threshold override silently ineffective, and a module docstring asserting a synthetic-data guarantee the code could not enforce. Most of these are now addressed.

**Reconciliation: what was found, then what was done.** Seven findings are fixed. Three are partially fixed. Seven are **accepted and documented rather than fixed**, because you chose safe fixes only and the caller could not be seen: keying the aggregation to a person, a business day and a direction would have changed both public signatures. That was the right call with an unknown caller, and it is why the verdict is still not-yet. Sixteen remain open, most of them compliance items that need a human, such as naming the threshold owner and filling the governance dates.

**One thing we caught on ourselves.** The first fix round introduced a data-safety regression: the new validation error messages interpolated the whole transaction record, which would have put customer data into tracebacks and logs. The original code never did that. Ravi found it on re-review, and Kenji fixed it in a second round. The error messages now name the record by its index and the field by name, never by value.

**Next steps, with my recommendation.**
1. **Recommended.** Answer the two open questions that block the rest: who owns this threshold, and does the calling job scope the input. Then commission the full fix for the aggregation, which needs signature changes and a caller inventory.
2. Put the file under version control before it governs any reporting decision. Nothing in this engagement could establish authorship, approval or change history, because none exists.
3. Grant execution consent so the 15 tests actually run. The QA verdict is currently inferred, not observed.
4. Have a human verify the 31 CFR citations against eCFR. Every one is marked TO-VERIFY.

I can carry out any of these. Say which.

## 1a. Iteration log

> 🔎 Review P1 (Ravi 12 · Layla 11) → 📊 Pip score → 🎩 Morgan challenge → ⛔ blocked on 3 user questions → 🔧 Fix R1 (Kenji) → 🧪 QA (Linh, static) + 🔎 Re-review P2 (Ravi) ❌ *(1 data-safety regression)* → 🔧 Fix R2 (Kenji) → 📊 Pip score → 🎩 Morgan verify

| 5 | 2026-09-14 | Morgan → user | 3 questions that change the correct fix | Answered. Safe fixes only, so 7 findings become accepted-not-fixed | state decisions |
| 6 | 2026-09-14 | Morgan → Kenji | Fix round 1 | 5 fixed, 3 partial, 15 tests written, not run | module + test file |
| 7 | 2026-09-14 | Morgan → Linh + Ravi | QA and re-review, concurrent | QA 🧠 inferred, DoD PARTIAL. Re-review: 10 new findings, no new critical, **RR-01 data-safety regression** | `qa-handover.md`, re-review pack |
| 8 | 2026-09-14 | Ravi → Kenji | RR-01 and RR-04 | Both fixed. Error messages no longer disclose record contents. `DAILY_LIMIT` retype reverted | module |
| 9 | 2026-09-14 | Morgan → Pip | Score the re-review pack | 13 found, 10 reported, 3 filtered, split confirmed, RR-01 confirmed never-filter | re-review envelope |

Pass 7's failure is kept on the record deliberately. A regression that was caught, routed, fixed and recorded is evidence the loop works.

## 2. Scope & what was delivered

Reviewed: `alert_threshold_check.py`, whole file, 19 lines as found. One Python file, the only source file in the project. Nothing excluded, so there is no unreviewed remainder.

Delivered: the module with safe fixes applied, a new `test_alert_threshold_check.py` with 15 tests, three findings packs, an independent QA handover, and this report.

Out of scope: the calling alerting job, the upstream data contract, any downstream case management. None of it exists in this project and none was supplied. Jurisdiction: **US (BSA / FinCEN) only**. EU, UK and NYDFS Part 504 were explicitly not assessed, on your confirmation that the institution is not New York regulated.

## 3. Requirements & traceability

N/A for a review. Worth stating plainly as a finding rather than an omission: **no RTM, no requirement id, no obligation reference and no specification exist anywhere in this project.** That is CMP-01 and it is open.

## 4. Code review

`Found 12 · Reported 12 · Filtered 0` on the first pass, `Found 13 · Reported 10 · Filtered 3` on the re-review. Deep depth, audit mode. Scored by Pip (`review-scorer`) in both cases, then challenged by me. Full detail with diffs and rationale is in the findings packs; this is the summary.

| Sev | Location | Issue | Basis | Status |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 🔴 Critical | `aggregate_daily` | Filters on neither date nor account nor person. Sums whatever list it is given (CR-01) | 📄 coded | **Accepted, documented not fixed** |
| 🔴 Critical | the accumulator line | Sums signed amounts, so a credit nets against a deposit and can suppress a reportable day (CR-02) | 📄 coded | **Accepted, documented not fixed** |
| 🟠 Warning | error messages | Validation messages interpolated the whole record into tracebacks and logs (RR-01, introduced by our own fix) | 📄 coded | **Fixed** |
| 🟠 Warning | `DAILY_LIMIT` | Bare untyped int, no unit, currency, rationale, owner or tuning date (CR-05) | 📄 coded | Partially fixed. Comment block added with placeholders; the values are yours to fill |
| 🟠 Warning | `txn["amount"]` | Unvalidated. Missing key, string, `None` or `bool` each mishandled (CR-04) | 📄 coded | Partially fixed. Validation added; RR-02 numpy scalars and RR-03 NaN remain |
| 🟠 Warning | whole module | No tests at all (CR-07) | 📊 measured | Partially fixed. 15 tests written, none executed |
| 🟠 Warning | `is_reportable` | Returns a bare bool, discarding the total, the limit applied and the count (CR-08) | 📄 coded | **Accepted, documented not fixed** |
| 🟠 Warning | both signatures | No type hints, no transaction data contract (CR-12) | 📊 measured, ruff | **Fixed** |
| 🟡 Medium | comparison line | Float accumulation deciding an exact monetary boundary (CR-03) | 🧠 inferred | **Fixed**, Decimal internally |
| 🟡 Medium | `limit=DAILY_LIMIT` | Import-time binding made a runtime threshold override silently ineffective (CR-10) | 📄 coded | **Fixed**, resolved at call time |
| 🟡 Medium | docstrings | Asserted a synthetic-data guarantee the code cannot enforce, and a scoping it does not implement (CR-11) | 📄 coded | **Fixed** |
| 🟡 Medium | empty input | An empty list is indistinguishable from a broken feed (CR-09) | 📄 coded | **Accepted, documented not fixed.** Raising would break unknown callers |
| 🔵 Style | comparison line | The strict `>` is **correct** and now carries a comment saying so. Recorded so nobody "fixes" it to `>=` (CR-06) | 📄 coded | **Fixed** |

Eight further re-review findings are open and are in the pack: numpy scalar rejection, NaN and Infinity passing validation, unfilled governance placeholders, no dependency manifest or CI, fail-stop batch validation with no quarantine, and two comments that overclaim.

**Architectural note.** The module conflates computing an aggregate with deciding a policy, and you confirmed it serves both a mandatory CTR filing determination and a discretionary investigation alert from one bool. Those carry different obligations and different error tolerance. Separating them is a signature change and is open.

**🔵 Developer guidance - improving future code.**
1. Put the aggregation key in the signature, not in the docstring. A function named for one day and one account should take that day and that account, so the contract is enforced rather than asserted.
2. Money is neither a float nor a bare int. Use `Decimal` or integer minor units from the edge of the system inward.
3. Write the boundary tests before the logic. The cases that decide this module are exactly at the limit, one cent either side, the empty list, a netting pair, and a record with no amount key.
4. When code makes a regulatory decision, return the evidence with the decision. A bare bool cannot be explained to an examiner six months later.

**🧑‍💻 Prompting guidance.** You told us the origin was mixed. Two findings here are classic AI-assisted shapes. CR-01 is the strongest example: the docstring described an aggregation that was never implemented, and it reads as correct precisely because the name supplies the missing logic to the reader. CR-02 is the same pattern at the data level, an unstated assumption that every amount is a same-direction positive. A prompt that said "the function must take the aggregation key as arguments and must not trust the caller to pre-filter" would have prevented both. When asking for detection logic, state the rule's qualifiers explicitly, entity, direction and window, rather than the headline number.

Review `alert_threshold_check.py`, a 19-line helper that decides whether one day's activity on
one account is reportable. Three specific questions:

1. Is the threshold defensible as written?

🧠 Inferred, not confirmed. The code carries no obligation reference of its own. A same-day
aggregate over one account against a hard `10000` limit is the shape of a cash-transaction
reporting threshold. Two candidates, both TO-VERIFY:

| Obligation | Jurisdiction | Article / rule | What it requires |
|---|---|---|---|
